messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED - Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts observed in us-east-1 ingress gateways. Initial alert threshold crossed at 12:03 UTC. Pager sent to oncall_bob and SRE rotation.

oncall_bob: seeing a big spike in 502/504s, dashboards show sawtooth pattern across multiple edge-pools. impact: higher latencies and ~3% of requests failing for a subset of customers.

maria: notable increase aligns with a deployment window? Checking deploybot.

incbot: deploybot: no recent production deploys in last 30m for gateway or proxy services.

aj: I can repro a request path getting long tails from ingress -> auth proxy -> route service. auth proxy logs show repeated upstream resets (RST).

sre_lead: oncall_bob, escalate if you need cross-region traffic shift. First thing: can we isolate blast radius by draining troubled edge-pools and steering to alternate pools in us-west-2?

oncall_bob: starting pool drain on pool-eus-3-edge-07 (small subset). will monitor error rate.

jordan: adding a temporary circuit-breaker rule at LB layer to reduce concurrent streams to auth-proxy behind that pool: config snippet I pushed:```yaml
circuit_breakers:
  max_connections: 500
  max_pending_requests: 100
  retry_budget: 10%
```

ops_runbook: NOTE: draining may increase latency for routed traffic. Suggest immediate CDN-level retry increase and client-facing 429->retry hints.

maria: support_chef, heads up for customers on managed tenants in us-east-1? Prepping comms.

support_chef: ACK. Drafting a short status note: "We are investigating increased API errors in us-east-1; engineers are actively mitigating and traffic is being routed to alternate regions. No data loss reported." Will post once we have concrete rollback/reroute.

aj: auth-proxy metrics: spikes in connect_retries and ECONNRESET from upstream ML workers cluster-proxy-01. CPU and sockets look fine, but backend keepalive drop rates up. Could be network flaps to mlworkers AZ-b instances.

sre_lead: can we fail over those particular routes to a healthy replica (mlworkers-b)? If not, we should fallback to the model-approx variant to keep clients served.

oncall_bob: initiating cross-region steer for traffic tagged as high-latency candidates. Using route policy: prefer us-west-2 region for new connections for route=llm-infer.

incbot: traffic-steer job started at 12:12 UTC. Estimated effect visible within 30s.

maria: patching routing policy with safe-rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 2m increments. Watch for error regression.

jordan: logs after first 25% shift: overall 5xx rate dropped from 2.9% -> 1.5% across global ingress. Targeted tenants show improvement.

aj: still seeing some 504s for long-lived streaming requests; these are hitting the same auth proxy connection limit. Might need to increase keepalive timeout on proxy or implement short-circuit for streaming to bypass auth on existing session tokens.

ops_runbook: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) Increase proxy keepalive to 90s (quick config); 2) add L7 retry for 502/504 up to 2 retries with backoff; 3) temporarily route streaming sessions to a dedicated pool.

oncall_bob: applying keepalive bump now (hotfix) to auth proxy config in us-east-1: `kubectl set env deployment/auth-proxy KEEPALIVE=90 --namespace=prod`.

incbot: hotfix deployed at 12:19 UTC to us-east-1 auth-proxy replicas.

maria: monitoring latency and errors... initial telemetry: streaming 504s dropped ~60% in affected tenants. Good signal.

support_chef: posting interim status update to support channel and to PD customers: "Partial outage in us-east-1 affecting a small portion of traffic; we've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations. Some streaming requests may experience transient errors or reconnects."

jordan: one notable customer (acct: acme-io) reported increased failures for long polling webhooks — assigned to the partner owner for follow-up.

aj: server-side postmortem note: upstream nodes in AZ-b had intermittent BFD flaps caused by top-of-rack switch firmware bug. Network team confirms ongoing investigation. This explains socket RST patterns.

sre_lead: mark incident severity P1 -> P0? We should keep P1 but escalate to network page. Paging network infra.

incbot: network-team paged at 12:28 UTC.

oncall_bob: summary so far: isolation + controlled cross-region steering + proxy keepalive bump + retry/backoff = error rate back to ~0.8% global, us-east-1 residual 0.9%. Streaming improved but not fully stable for long-lived sessions.

maria: next steps: 1) network remediation from infra, 2) permanent routing policy to avoid the bad AZ for a week, 3) run a cold restart of the affected mlworker set during low traffic window, 4) support to send personalized notes to customers who hit repeated failures.

support_chef: will compile list of affected tenants and owners for outreach.

jordan: will schedule the restart and coordinate maintenance window.

sre_lead: create a post-incident action item: ensure graceful backoff for streaming client library, and add health-check improvements to detect upstream BFD flaps earlier.

maria: posting public status page update in 10m. Also, debrief meeting at 13:00 UTC with SRE, network, api-platform, and support to sync on RCA and customer comms.

incbot: INCIDENT CLOSURE RECOMMENDED - error rates stable under SLO, routing circumvented failing AZ. Recommend follow-up: RCA, firmware rollback/patch by network, and permanent routing policy update.

oncall_bob: acknowledging. I will hand off to next oncall at shift change; see brief in #oncall-handoff. :thumbsup:

support_chef: final note: no customer data loss; some clients experienced reconnects. Keeping incident open for RCA tracking until patch applied.

incbot: incident status -> under-review. closed_at: 12:44 UTC (mitigation in place).

maria: thanks everyone. Good coordination.
